body_swap:

subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the [CHARACTER] shown in <Picture 1> (a character sheet with a close-up face portrait and front, side and back views).

<Subject 2> is the [PERSON] in <Video 1>, whose pose, actions, motion, timing, and interaction with the environment must be followed.

<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit, providing the original performance, motion, camera movement, framing, timing, lighting, environment, scene composition, and temporal structure.

summary:

[video editing + reference generation]

The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace <Subject 2> completely with <Subject 1> from the character sheet <Picture 1>, keeping the complete appearance of <Subject 1> and the performance of <Subject 2>. Preserve the source video's camera behavior, environment, lighting, timing, and composition.

detailed_description:

<Subject 1> takes the place of <Subject 2> and performs the same motion, pose, gestures, actions, speed, and timing throughout <Video 1>, while keeping the complete look from the character sheet <Picture 1>: [CHARACTER]. Maintain strong temporal consistency. Prevent identity drift, outfit changes, flickering, or frame-to-frame inconsistency. Do not alter the background, objects, environment, camera trajectory, framing, or composition inherited from <Video 1>.

overall_soundscape:

Preserve the original audio of <Video 1>.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist. This is the Reference to Video version of MiniMax H3 (ref2va), the one that can look at pictures and videos you give it.

READ LICENSE More versions 

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors14.6 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

Qwen3-VL 32B reads your prompt AND looks at your pictures and video. It works on any recent NVIDIA card, not only the newest.

 Load VAE (video and sound)

Download minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.6 GB  

Download minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors577 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 The int8 video VAE is about twice as fast as the older fp16 one and looks the same. The fp16 one from earlier episodes still works if you already have it.

 LoRAs (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

The speed LoRA (DMAD 4-step, by Kijai): 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

Download minimax_h3_DMAD_4step_full_lora_avg_rank_39_bf16.safetensors350 MB  

The Character Swap LoRA by Alissonerdx: teaches H3 to put the person from your picture into the video.

Download minimax_h3_character_swap_v1.0_ref2va_r64_gl.safetensors592 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

The swap, head, style, VFX and sharpness LoRAs are made by Alissonerdx. Free to use, also for paid videos; read the licence on the page.

Alissonerdx LoRAs and licence 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Swaps the person in a video for your character. The room, the light, the camera, every move and the original voice and music stay; only the person changes.

 Steps

  1. 1. Pick how many seconds of your video to use (5 s is a good start).
  2. 2. Leave the size at 480 x 864 (portrait for Shorts, landscape for a wide video). The swap holds best at this size.
  3. 3. Load your video. One person in the shot works best.
  4. 4. Load your character, best as a character sheet (see below).
  5. 5. In Find and Replace, describe your character (the [PERSON] box can stay as it is). See below.
  6. Press Run.

 The character picture

  • A character sheet works best: a face close-up plus the whole body from the front, side and back, on a plain grey or white background. Workflow 1 makes one from a single picture.
  • Pick a character with a similar build to the person in the video (a man for a man, a woman for a woman). A very different body can make the swap start late: the original person stays for the first second and then changes.
  • Keep the background plain: a busy background in the picture can leak into the video.

 The 2 boxes to fill in

  • [CHARACTER]: your character in a few words, the hair, the clothes, the colours: young woman with red hair in a white space suit. It goes into the prompt twice, which made the swap start on the first frame in the tests.
  • [PERSON]: leave person in the video (it worked as well as a full description in the tests). Only with several people in the video, point yours out: woman in the green sweater.
  • Leave the long prompt as it is: the swap LoRA was trained on exactly this layout.

 Good to know

  • Waist-up and talking clips swap most cleanly; a closer shot gives a bigger, cleaner face. A whole body works too.
  • Want it sharp and Full HD? Workflow 3 (Character Swap + Upscale to Full HD) swaps at 480 and then sharpens to 1080 x 1920 in the same Run. Swapping straight at a bigger size sometimes kept the original person in the tests.
  • Up to 15 seconds: over 10 s takes longer and needs more graphics card memory. In the tests a 10 second clip at 480 x 864 took about 2 minutes (108 s) and kept the whole costume to the end.
  • A cartoon or a mascot instead of a person? Use workflow 5: this one keeps a human body shape.
  • Did the first frames keep the original person, or does a ghost of them show? Try another seed, a closer character sheet, or a character more like the person in the video.
  • The person in your video already LOOKS like your character (the same hair colour, a beard)? H3 may keep them as they are: in the tests only 1 seed of 3 swapped such a man into a knight, while a clearly different character swapped on every seed. Try 2 or 3 seeds, or pick a character that looks clearly different.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed + character swap) - Holds two LoRAs and both stay ON: the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA (4 steps instead of 20) and the Character Swap LoRA (puts the person from your picture into the video). Strength 1 for both: a higher swap strength left a see-through ghost of the original person in the tests.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Duration Pixaroma (1. how many seconds) - How many seconds to use from your video, turned into the frame count H3 accepts.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. video size) - The size of the new video. 480 x 864 is the default: the swap holds best there (in the tests 480 swapped from the first frame on every clip; at 576 and bigger it was a lottery: sometimes from the start, sometimes 2 to 3 seconds late, once not at all, and more steps did not help). For sharp Full HD, use workflow 3 (Character Swap + Upscale to Full HD): it swaps at this size, then sharpens. The Portrait / Landscape switch must match YOUR video: portrait for a portrait video, landscape for a landscape one. Your video is cropped to this shape, so the other one cuts away part of it. Every size here is a multiple of 32, which H3 needs.
  • Load Video Pixaroma (3. your video) - Your video, the one whose person gets replaced. It is cropped to the size from step 2 (nothing stretched) and cut to the seconds from step 1. Its sound goes straight to the saved video, so the voice and music stay the original.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (4. your character) - Your character. A character sheet works best: a face close-up plus the whole body from the front, side and back, on a plain background (workflow 1 makes one from a single picture). A busy background in this picture can leak into the video.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the swap prompt, leave it) - The long prompt in the layout the LoRA was trained on. Leave it as it is: the words in [BRACKETS] are filled in from the Find and Replace node above.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (5. your character + the person to replace) - [CHARACTER] = your character in a few words (it goes into the prompt twice, which made the swap start on the first frame in the tests). [PERSON] can stay person in the video: in the tests it swapped exactly like a full description. Describe the person only when your video has more than one.
  • Seed Pixaroma (6. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + your character) - Builds the empty video at your size and length, and reads the prompt together with your character picture (<Picture 1> in the prompt).
  • MiniMaxH3AddGuide (your video, from frame 0) - Lays your source video (and its sound) over the new video, frame by frame from the first frame. This is what keeps the room, the camera, the timing and every move of the original.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the swapped video) - Saves the new video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Character Swap with the ORIGINAL sound of your video, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Size5 seconds
480 x 864about 1 min (57 s)
576 x 1024about 1.5 min (75 s)
704 x 1280about 2 min (130 s)

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
